<solution_file path="src/t02_load_eurostat.py">
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import csv
import os
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd


def main() -> None:
    # Define file paths relative to the current working directory (workspace root)
    selected = Path("outputs") / "t01_selected_indicators.csv"
    raw = Path("inputs") / "eurostat" / "eurostat_city_values_sample.csv"
    out = Path("outputs") / "t02_eurostat_raw.csv"

    # Load selected indicator ids
    selected_ids = pd.read_csv(
        selected,
        usecols=["indicator_id"],
        dtype={"indicator_id": str},
    ).squeeze()

    # Load raw Eurostat city values
    raw_df = pd.read_csv(
        raw,
        dtype={
            "city_id": str,
            "city_name": str,
            "year": int,
            "indicator_id": str,
            "indicator_name": str,
            "theme": str,
            "unit": str,
        },
        usecols=[
            "city_id",
            "city_name",
            "year",
            "indicator_id",
            "indicator_name",
            "value",
            "unit",
        ],
    )

    # Keep only the selected indicators
    raw_df = raw_df[raw_df["indicator_id"].isin(selected_ids)]

    # Only numeric values – drop rows where value is NaN
    raw_df = raw_df.dropna(subset=["value"])

    # Remove duplicate (city_id, year, indicator_id) – keep first
    raw_df = raw_df.drop_duplicates(
        subset=["city_id", "year", "indicator_id"],
        keep="first",
    )

    # Ensure correct column order and names
    out_cols = [
        "city_id",
        "city_name",
        "year",
        "indicator_id",
        "indicator_name",
        "value",
        "unit",
    ]
    raw_df = raw_df[out_cols]

    # Write CSV with RFC 4180 compliance: quote only when necessary
    raw_df.to_csv(
        out,
        index=False,
        quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL,
    )

    print(f"Wrote {len(raw_df)} rows to {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
</solution_file>
